title: Round 1 sealed investigation:  universal transformations of ECDLP instances
question: Can an arbitrary ECDLP instance (E/F_q, P, Q=[k]P) be transformed, in time polynomial (ideally quasi-linear) in input length, into an equivalent instance of a problem with additional exploitable structure, with efficient solution recovery? Characterize the requirements on such a transformation and explain precisely why known restricted-case transfers (MOV/FR pairings, anomalous/SSSA lifts, GHS Weil descent, summation-polynomial index calculus, isogeny walks) do not generalize.

claims: B1 (elementary): hom from prime-order cyclic group is trivial or injective; nontrivial hom into finite T forces r | |T|; into F_Q^* iff r | Q-1; into (F_Q,+) iff r=p; torsion-free targets trivial.
B2 (elementary): Pohlig-Hellman-style smooth-order targets cannot receive a nontrivial image of an order-r group with r larger than the smoothness bound.
B3 (elementary proof, finite check only): at most M(M+1) Frobenius traces t give #E with a prime factor r>4*sqrt(q) and ord_r(q)<=M; numerical check for p up to 80021 found 1-3 such traces for M=6.
B4: for r != p, the r-torsion lifts uniquely into E(Q_p)[r], where additive p-adic maps vanish; the anomalous attack uses r=p essentially (standard facts, not re-derived).
B5: every algebraic morphism from an elliptic curve to an affine algebraic group is constant (proper vs affine).
B6: Frobenius-equivariant maps from an F-fixed point P into a character twist c force (1-c)f(P)=0; unifies MOV (c=q^k), anomalous (r=p).
B7: isogeny classes share #E (Tate), so isogeny transfers cannot repair MOV or anomalous obstructions.
B8-B11 are conjectures/open requirements (cover genus regime, approximate characters, factor-base definability for prime fields); no proof.
Experiments: 1498 curves over p in [1000,3000), mean ord_r(p)/r = 0.58 (non-anomalous); hom-count check gcd(r,q-1) had 0 mismatches; Lean sketches uncompiled.
Nothing here proves or refutes the universal O(n log n) ECDLP objective.
